name: Entraygues - Le Fel

limits: For red and rosé wine, Fer: at least 50%
For red and rosé wine, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon together: at least 10%
For red and rosé wine, Mouyssagues and Négret de Banhars together: at most 15%
For white wine, Chenin Blanc: at least 90%
rules.yield_base: 55 hl/ha for red, 60 for white and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Cahors's limestone soils give Malbec its darkest and most tannic form.
Madiran, from Tannat, is typically very concentrated and high in tannin.
Bergerac reds are often dark and full bodied.
Jurançon makes a dry white and a more sought-after sweet white with tropical fruit aromas.

blurb.text: A South West France appellation of eight communes, making wine from Fer for red and Chenin for white. Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and a few other grapes are allowed too.
